tourist_licence_phase_out.title: Tourist-flat licence phase-out
tourist_licence_phase_out.jurisdiction: Catalonia (municipalities with housing-access problems, Barcelona included)
tourist_licence_phase_out.rule: Existing tourist flats (HUT) in the affected municipalities must obtain an urban-planning licence within 5 years of the decree, or stop operating.
exceptions: Owners can request one extension of up to 5 more years, after year 4 and before the period ends (transitional provision 1.2).
tourist_licence_phase_out.law: Decret llei 3/2023, de 7 de novembre (DOGC 9036, 8 Nov 2023)
tourist_licence_phase_out.status: In force. Ratified by the Catalan Parliament on 20 Dec 2023; the constitutional challenge was dismissed in full (STC 64/2025, 13 Mar 2025).
tourist_licence_phase_out.notes: The 9 Nov 2028 date ends the regional transition. Barcelona's council has said it does not plan to grant the new licences (press reports from June 2024, not re-checked), so most licences are expected to lapse. That is a stated policy, not a legal text.
tourist_licence_phase_out.data_limits: Which flats will obtain a licence or an extension, and what the others become after 2028: long-term homes, seasonal lets, sales or listings on other platforms. A stable register before a deadline says nothing about whether the policy will work, and a cancelled tourist use does not show conversion to a residential lease.

rent_cap.title: Rent limit in stressed zones
rent_cap.jurisdiction: Spain; applied in the Catalan zones declared by the Generalitat
rent_cap.rule: In a declared stressed zone, a new housing lease cannot exceed the last rent of the previous five years (after its annual update). Large landlords are limited by the reference-index maximum instead (LAU art. 17.6 and 17.7).
exceptions: Up to +10% over the previous rent when the flat was recently renovated or improved, or the lease runs 10 years or more.
A flat with no lease in the last five years is limited by the index only where the ministry's resolution for that zone says so.
rent_cap.law: Ley 12/2023, de 24 de mayo; LAU art. 17.6-7; Resolució TER/800/2024 (Catalan zones)
rent_cap.status: In force. The zone is valid for 3 years from 16 Mar 2024 and has been extended for 118 municipalities by Resolució TER/3739/2026 (DOGC 19 Oct 2026).
rent_cap.notes: Barcelona is on the Generalitat's technical list for the extension; the extension's end date was not checked.
rent_cap.data_limits: Whether the limit caused any change. The average rent moves with the mix of flats rented, and interest rates, wages and supply move rents at the same time. Compliance of individual contracts is not visible either.

seasonal_rentals.title: Rent limit extended to seasonal lets
seasonal_rentals.rule: In a stressed zone, a seasonal let that is not for exclusively holiday or leisure use is treated as a housing lease, so the same rent limits apply. The rents of simultaneous room contracts cannot exceed the maximum for the whole flat.
exceptions: Lets for exclusively recreational, tourist or holiday use are outside the rule (new art. 66 bis of Llei 18/2007).
seasonal_rentals.status: In force. A constitutional challenge was admitted for processing on 9 Jun 2026 (recurso 2415-2026, against arts. 2.2, 3.8, 5.5, 5.6, 5.8, 5.9, 5.14, 5.15 and 8.1). No ruling was found as of the check date; the sources checked do not mention a suspension.
seasonal_rentals.data_limits: Whether seasonal lets respect the limit (that needs each flat's size and the official index), how long guests actually stay, and whether the winter dip after January is the law or an ordinary seasonal pattern.

owners_vote_catalonia.title: Owners' vote on tourist use: Catalonia
owners_vote_catalonia.jurisdiction: Catalonia (its own Civil Code regime for horizontal property)
owners_vote_catalonia.rule: Restricting tourist use through a community's statutes means changing the statutes, which needs the votes of 4/5 of the owners who also hold 4/5 of the participation shares (Catalan Civil Code art. 553-26.2.a).
exceptions: The article applies unless a legal provision says otherwise; any Catalan tourism-specific provision was not exhaustively searched.
owners_vote_catalonia.law: Llei 5/2006, llibre cinquè del Codi civil de Catalunya, art. 553-26
owners_vote_catalonia.status: In force (book five in force since 1 Jul 2006; article checked as consolidated).

sources.label: Catalan Civil Code, book five (BOE, consolidated)

owners_vote_catalonia.notes: That the national three-fifths rule does not apply in Catalonia, and that a ban only reaches new tourist licences, is reported by Catalan press (3Cat, VilaWeb, Betevé) and a Generalitat legal analysis; the statute text itself gives the 4/5 majority.
owners_vote_catalonia.data_limits: Anything at building level. The files have no data on owners' associations or their votes.

owners_approval_spain.title: Owners' approval of tourist lets: rest of Spain
owners_approval_spain.jurisdiction: Spain, Ley de Propiedad Horizontal (applies to Madrid, Valencia, Málaga and Sevilla)
owners_approval_spain.rule: A new tourist let needs the community's prior express approval. Approving, limiting, conditioning or prohibiting tourist lets takes 3/5 of the owners who also hold 3/5 of the shares (LPH arts. 5.3 and 17.12, as amended by LO 1/2025).
exceptions: Lets already operating before 3 Apr 2025 under the tourist rules can continue (additional provision 2).
owners_approval_spain.law: Ley Orgánica 1/2025, de 2 de enero (BOE 3 Jan 2025), amending the LPH
owners_approval_spain.data_limits: Anything at building level. The files have no data on owners' associations or their votes.

post_observation_developments.title: Real Decreto-ley 29/2026: urgent housing measures
post_observation_developments.summary: Amends the national tenancy law (LAU) on temporary and room rentals: a temporary lease needs a real, provable reason for the tenant to live away from their habitual home. It also caps annual rent increases until 31 Dec 2027.
post_observation_developments.note: Published after every snapshot used here, so it cannot explain any change in the data. Summary read from the BOE page; the full text and its parliamentary validation were not reviewed.

sources.title: Ajuntament de Barcelona - Habitatges d'ús turístic
Generalitat de Catalunya - Preu mitjà del lloguer (Incasòl)

caveats: Prices are asking prices, not what guests paid; every Dec 2025 snapshot has no prices.

The population is listings with at least one open date in the next 365 days. An empty calendar can mean booked, blocked or withdrawn, and listings with no open dates jump to ~22-24% in every city's Sep 2026 snapshot. The 31+ share in Barcelona is 41.7% / 41.5% / 39.9% under three population definitions (see the note under the first chart).
A listing that is absent from a later scrape may have been withdrawn, re-listed under a new id, or missed by the scrape.
Tourist-licence shares outside Catalonia are a lower bound: only confirmed regional codes are counted.
A missing or unmatched licence number is not proof of an illegal listing.
Airbnb's licence form changed: the 'Exempt - seasonal rental' option first appears in Jun 2026, so licence categories are not comparable across that date.
Comparisons show timing and differences, not causes.
